caption:
The video captures a barefoot female dancer in a black crop top and long flowing skirt performing inside a dusty, abandoned hall lined with fluted concrete columns. A rectangular patch of daylight falls on the tiled floor, with a faded reddish wall and a small window anchoring the right. She is already mid-rotation, torso partly back-facing, arms bent near her head, hair and skirt flaring outward.

The turn shifts her torso to side-facing as her hair whips around, and she folds forward at the waist, reaching both arms out in front with the skirt draping around her legs. While bent, her arms swing to extended sideways, hands blurring with motion. She rises into a right-side profile, lifting one arm overhead and extending the other, raising one foot off the floor. Then she arches backward, one arm thrust high overhead, the other down toward the floor, a leg extended sideways.

She settles into a low floor lunge and backbend, trailing leg extended, foot on the ground, torso arched back, head tilted, one arm stretched upward. This pose is held to the end of the clip with only small changes in arm angle.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
